data.content:
❓ Exchange eligibility, tuition waivers, credit conversion, visa rules, and application routes depend heavily on your home university, citizenship, degree stage, timing, and language credentials. If an item is unknown, enter “unknown.”

To produce a shortlist that is genuinely eligible, credit-transferable, and affordable—not just a generic comparison—please provide the following details.

  1. Current university, school/department, and degree program (required)
  2. Degree level and current year (required) — options: Master’s—Year 1 / Master’s—Year 2 or later / PhD—Year 1 / PhD—Year 2 or later / Other
  3. Passport citizenship / region (required)
  4. Preferred term and year (required)
  5. Acceptable program formats (required) — options: Course-based semester exchange / Research visiting student / lab placement / Summer/winter school with transferable credit / Hybrid coursework plus supervised research (multiple allowed)
  6. Known home-university requirements for credit recognition
  7. Known overseas partner universities or exchange-program webpage
  8. Primary academic goal (required) — options: New-media technology coursework / Public-opinion / computational communication research / Methods training (Python/data/AI) / Thesis or dissertation progress / Academic networking / PhD preparation / Industry and policy exposure / Cross-cultural experience (multiple allowed)
  9. Language ability and test scores (required)
  10. Approximate GPA/average and notable research experience
  11. Maximum total out-of-pocket budget for one term (required)
  12. Funding requirement (required) — options: Must be fully or almost fully funded / Need substantial scholarship support / Partial funding preferred but not essential / Can self-fund within stated budget
  13. Other constraints or preferences

Please reply with a value for each field.

messages.content:
<system-reminder>
<current_date>2026-09-15, Tuesday</current_date>
</system-reminder>

Research and compare academically legitimate overseas exchange or short-term visiting programs that can be completed within one semester and can satisfy ordinary credit and academic requirements.

Compare options in the United States, Europe, Japan and Singapore. Cover curriculum and teaching models, credit transfer, academic environment, living costs, visa and language requirements, scholarships or financial aid, research and networking value, cross-cultural value and practical adaptation issues.

Produce a prioritized shortlist and preparation plan.

Available user profile context (incomplete):
- [IDENTITY / EDUCATION] Graduate work focuses on new-media technology and public-opinion analysis.
- [IDENTITY / EDUCATION] Grew up in Beijing; values social responsibility and personal fulfillment.
- [FAMILY] Lives with parents in a harmonious family.
- [FAMILY] Father is a civil servant: rigorous, rule-oriented.
- [LIVING ENVIRONMENT] Grew up with strong access to educational/cultural resources, fostering interest in current affairs and social issues.
- [DIGITAL / ACADEMIC BEHAVIOR] Roughly 1.5 hours/day on news/trending topics.
- [DIGITAL / ACADEMIC BEHAVIOR] Proficient with Word, Excel and Python for research/content work.
- [ROUTINE / TIME] Recently spends more on coffee beans/brewing equipment but remains rational overall.
- [ROUTINE / TIME] Prefers evenings for reading/reflection; mornings for light exercise/breakfast.
- [ROUTINE / TIME] Often visits university library, parks and music cafes; recently started weekly gym visits.
- [PERSONALITY / DECISION STYLE] Calm, critical thinker, analytical and observant.
- [PERSONALITY / DECISION STYLE] Likes getting to the essence of problems.
- [PERSONALITY / DECISION STYLE] Makes decisions independently but considers authoritative opinions.
- [PERSONALITY / DECISION STYLE] Good listener; communicates complex issues clearly.
- [LIFESTYLE / CONSUMPTION] Shops online for convenience.
- [TRAVEL] Travels 2–3 times/year, mainly during holidays.
- [CONTENT / CULTURE] Saves articles about social issues, technology and communication research.
- [CONTENT / CULTURE] Watches documentaries, academic lectures and outdoor/travel videos.
- [CONTENT / CULTURE] Reads nonfiction and sociology; interested in Haruki Murakami.
- [CONTENT / CULTURE] Likes thoughtful opinions and culturally rich content.
- [HEALTH] Runs twice/week (~4 km each).
- [HEALTH] Does yoga; occasional badminton.
- [HEALTH] Healthy overall; academic stress managed through exercise/meditation/music.
- [FINANCE] Income mainly scholarships and part-time writing/submissions.
- [FINANCE] Some savings and study equipment; no debt.

<current_date>2026-09-15, Tuesday</current_date>

Research and compare academically legitimate overseas exchange or short-term visiting programs that can be completed within one semester and can satisfy ordinary credit and academic requirements.

messages.content:
❓ Exchange eligibility, tuition waivers, credit conversion, visa rules, and application routes depend heavily on your home university, citizenship, degree stage, timing, and language credentials. If an item is unknown, enter “unknown.”

To produce a shortlist that is genuinely eligible, credit-transferable, and affordable—not just a generic comparison—please provide the following details.

  1. Current university, school/department, and degree program (required)
  2. Degree level and current year (required) — options: Master’s—Year 1 / Master’s—Year 2 or later / PhD—Year 1 / PhD—Year 2 or later / Other
  3. Passport citizenship / region (required)
  4. Preferred term and year (required)
  5. Acceptable program formats (required) — options: Course-based semester exchange / Research visiting student / lab placement / Summer/winter school with transferable credit / Hybrid coursework plus supervised research (multiple allowed)
  6. Known home-university requirements for credit recognition
  7. Known overseas partner universities or exchange-program webpage
  8. Primary academic goal (required) — options: New-media technology coursework / Public-opinion / computational communication research / Methods training (Python/data/AI) / Thesis or dissertation progress / Academic networking / PhD preparation / Industry and policy exposure / Cross-cultural experience (multiple allowed)
  9. Language ability and test scores (required)
  10. Approximate GPA/average and notable research experience
  11. Maximum total out-of-pocket budget for one term (required)
  12. Funding requirement (required) — options: Must be fully or almost fully funded / Need substantial scholarship support / Partial funding preferred but not essential / Can self-fund within stated budget
  13. Other constraints or preferences

Please reply with a value for each field.
